## Overview

Six Supabase Auth emails, authored as react-email components and shipped as static HTML.

- Sign up (`confirmation`) and sign in (`magic_link`) use the OTP code only, no links.
- `recovery`, `email_change`, and `invite` use a button link (plus the code where it applies).
- `reauthentication` is code only.

Brand styling lives in `emails/components/theme.ts` (the app's oklch tokens resolved to static hex, since email clients cannot use CSS variables) and `emails/components/brand-layout.tsx` (the shared shell). Dark theme. The logo is hardcoded to `https://wowlab.gg/logo.png` because email clients need an absolute PNG.

Supabase Go variables (`{{ .Token }}`, `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`, etc.) are written as literal strings in the templates and pass through render untouched.

## Preview and edit

```bash
pnpm email:dev   # from repo root, react-email preview on :3001
```

Edit the `emails/*.tsx` templates and the shared pieces in `emails/components/`.

## Deploy

```bash
SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=... SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF=... pnpm email:deploy
```

`email:deploy` runs `packages/emails/scripts/deploy.mts`: it renders the templates to `out/`, then `PATCH`es only the `mailer_templates_*` and `mailer_subjects_*` fields on the project's auth config via the Supabase Management API. It does not touch SMTP, redirect URLs, providers, or any other auth setting. We do not use `supabase config push`, which overwrites the entire auth config.

Both `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` are required. Create the access token on the [account tokens page](https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens).
